candidates.label: Actually dispose evidence and revoke provider access, then repeat both operations to prove idempotence
evidence: The repository contract supports consent_revocation evidence disposition and provider-access revocation.
Memory and PostgreSQL validations prove disposed then already_absent behavior.
Provider revocation deletes tokens and disconnects the provider account while intentionally preserving runner profile and disconnected account metadata; that residue is explicit in this option.

candidates.label: Perform only a deletion dry-run and leave the evidence row
rejectionReasons: No typed dry-run operation or dry-run receipt contract exists in the accepted implementation.
Leaving evidence after consent revocation contradicts the implemented consent_revocation disposition path.

candidates.label: Erase evidence, tokens, provider account metadata, and runner profile
rejectionReasons: The accepted repository contract intentionally preserves runner profile and disconnected provider-account metadata and provides no full-identity erasure operation.

candidates.label: Defer consent-revocation selection
evidence: Deferral performs no external effect and leaves the witness blocked.

candidates.label: Stop the real-witness sequence
evidence: Stopping requires no revocation or disposition operation.
